data.claim: A plain review of a gate with a recorded REVIEWED review can use the existing --delta machinery; a non-ancestor reviewed head must fall back to full
data.falsifier: a rebased branch producing a delta, or a merged record losing a triage
data.mechanism: reviewed_head evidence (from B-review-budget-rounds) + git merge-base --is-ancestor; triage is keyed by finding digest so merging by digest keeps verdicts
data.question: Does a delta re-review by default keep findings triaged and fall back safely after a rebase?

chunk_findings.detail: `"review_kind": kind if counted or kind != "full" else "full_unavailable"` only maps an unreviewed *full* round to the "unavailable" marker. For a delta round that never reached a reviewer (`status` is neither `R.REVIEWED` nor `R.PARTIAL` — e.g. the reviewer errors, the diff cannot be produced, or the run aborts), `kind == "delta"` so the expression returns `"delta"`, while `delta_rounds` is *not* incremented (because `reviewed` is false) yet `reviewed_head` is still set to the current HEAD. Concretely: gate has a recorded full round at H0; a delta run for `H0..H1` fails before a reviewer sees anything; the evidence now says `review_kind="delta"`, `delta_rounds` unchanged, `reviewed_head=H1`. A later `ddflow review <id> --gate G` computes its base from this recorded head, so the next delta covers `H1..H2` and the commits in `H0..H1` are never reviewed by anyone, with no marker that a delta was skipped and no reason for the rebase/anomaly fallback to fire. The full path deliberately avoids this by writing `full_unavailable`, and the delta path needs the analogous marker (or must fall back to a full round / leave `reviewed_head` where it was) when a delta does not reach a reviewer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py: _round_evidence (review_kind / delta_rounds)

chunk_findings.detail: `_last_review` is documented — and its sibling `_last_head` is documented — to honor that "a re-claim or `gate skip` replaces the gate's current record", but its loop does not: it walks past any gate event whose evidence has no `reviewed_head` and returns the *superseded* review's evidence instead. Concrete sequence: (1) a full review of `X.G` at head `H1` records evidence `{reviewed_head: H1, status: "REVIEWED"}`; (2) `ddflow gate X.G skip` (or a re-claim) appends a newer `gate.*` event for gate `G` whose evidence carries no `reviewed_head`; (3) `ddflow review X --gate G` with the shipped default `[review].delta_default = true` calls `_wants_delta` → `_last_review`, which skips step 2's event, returns step 1's evidence (`H1`, `REVIEWED`), finds `H1` is an ancestor of the tip, and returns `True` (delta). The gate's current record, however, is the skip, so the delta is unsound. `_delta_scope` computes its base via `_last_head`, which per its own docstring honors the replacement and yields `""`, so the plain re-review fails with "run the full review first" instead of performing the full round the fallback path is supposed to produce; if `_delta_scope` also walked past the skip, the review would instead cover only `H1..tip`, leaving the pre-`H1` diff unreviewed — precisely the failure the new fallback message warns about. `_last_review` needs to stop at the newest `gate.*` record for the gate and return `{}` unless that record is itself a review (i.e. mirror `_last_head`'s replacement semantics), not scan for the newest event that happens to carry a `reviewed_head`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_last_review (used by `_wants_delta`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The new evidence key `"full": full` records the *user-supplied flag* `full`, not the *actual round type* that ran. `review()` never writes the true round kind into this field — the actual kind is carried by `kind`/`_round_evidence`/`_delta_rounds`, and this parameter stays at its default `False` on every path where the round is full without the literal `--full` flag being passed.

Concrete inputs that make it wrong:

1. Project has `[review].delta_default = true` and the gate has a recorded review. The branch is rebased so the recorded head is no longer an ancestor of HEAD, so the intended behaviour is "falls back to a full round". The caller invokes `review(..., full=False)` (the user did not pass `--full`); the code takes the full path but writes `"full": False` into the evidence. Any consumer that reads `evidence["full"]` — which is exactly what the acceptance criterion "the gate status shows full rounds and delta rounds separately" implies — counts this full round as a delta round, so full/delta round accounting (and the `max_rounds` budget the evidence feeds) is wrong.

2. Project has `[review].delta_default = false` (every plain review is a full round). Every such review records `"full": False` because the flag was never set, so the recorded "round kind" is the opposite of what actually ran.

This is also the "second evidence field" the task explicitly warned against: the round/full-delta flag is supposed to come from the B-review-budget-rounds evidence field (rb-rounds), and this line invents a parallel field whose value can disagree with the real round kind (and with that other flag), producing inconsistent counts. Recording the flag instead of resolving it to the actual round kind (as `_round_evidence`/`kind` already do) is the defect; the field should reflect the round that ran, or be omitted in favour of the shared flag.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py (evidence dict, `"full": full`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_wants_delta` treats every call that does not set `chunks`, `commit`, `base`, or `full` as "plain", so an explicit `--force` is converted into a delta whenever `[review].delta_default` is on and a prior `REVIEWED` head is an ancestor of HEAD. Because the caller only evaluates `_budget` when `kind == "full"`, the `force` (and `reason`) argument is then never consulted: running `ddflow review X --gate G --force` after the gate has hit `[review].max_rounds` no longer produces the forced full round it produced before this change (and which the budget-refusal text tells the user to request); it silently produces a delta instead — e.g. with no new commits since the recorded head it prints "delta review of 0 commits since <sha>", merges that (empty) delta into the gate record, and leaves the full-round count at the cap. `--force` alone needs to be treated as non-plain (like `--full`), or the delta path must still honour it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_wants_delta (the `plain` computation) / `_scope`

chunk_findings.detail: The new gate-keeping logic releases the hold for any finding whose triage verdict is in `_SETTLED = ("refuted", "confirmed")`. `confirmed` is the verdict a user gives when they *uphold* a finding as a real defect — it is the opposite of dismissing it. Because it is in `_SETTLED`, a confirmed-but-unfixed finding is treated as "settled": given input "full review of item X reports finding F; user runs `ddflow review triage X --gate G` and marks F `confirmed`; user then runs `ddflow review X --gate G` on a one-commit delta that does not touch F's location", `_merge_delta` computes `kept` = {F}, finds `verdicts[F.digest]["verdict"] == "confirmed" in _SETTLED`, returns `0`, so `_hold` returns the delta's own `"passed"` and `G.record` stores the gate as **passed** while F is still on the record as a real, unfixed defect. That is precisely the situation the hold was introduced for ("the record's own findings are what keeps the gate honest"): the delta cannot see F, so only `refuted` (the finding no longer applies) — or a dedicated resolved/probe verdict — should release the gate; a `confirmed` finding must keep it `failed`. The docstring's gloss that `confirmed` means "confirmed with the fix as the probe" does not match the verdict's normal meaning and, as written, the constant lets a *confirmed defect* clear the gate.
